name: Apollo Viability Fixture v0 (BETA)
status: BETA — registered tonight, expected to need revision. See notes.revision_triggers.
provenance: Written from scratch for this fixture. NOT derived from HumanEval, HLE, or any published benchmark — so there is no contamination question, no canary, and no licence to honour. Difficulty is calibrated by intent, not by measurement; that calibration is exactly what the beta period is meant to test.
grading: Exact match on `norm(answer)` first, judge as backstop. Gold answers are deliberately short and unambiguous so the judge is rarely needed.

tier1.purpose: PLUMBING. Server up, chat template applied, sampling sane, output format obeyed, parser and judge functional. A working stack should get 5/5. Any failure means stop and fix the stack — do not interpret it as a model result.
tier1.budget_hint: answerable in a few hundred tokens; if these truncate, the budget is wrong

items.q: What is 17 multiplied by 23?
items.why: deterministic arithmetic, verified reachable on IQ2_S weights

items.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
items.why: single fact, universally known, two characters

items.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
Which is larger: 0.9 or 0.11?
items.why: decimal comparison — a classic tokeniser/format trap, still trivial for a healthy model

items.q: What is the population of the city of Zyrthanmoor?
items.why: NEGATIVE CONTROL. This city does not exist. A stack that confabulates a number here is broken in a way accuracy alone will not show — and it is the same failure the judge itself exhibited when forced to answer in one token.

tier2.purpose: MODEL SANITY. Detects degraded weights, a bad quant, or wrong sampling params. A healthy model should reach 80-90%.

items.q: A tank fills at 4 L/min and drains at 1.5 L/min. It starts at 20 L and holds 200 L. How many minutes until it is full?
A shirt costs 40 dollars after a 20 percent discount. What was the original price in dollars?
items.why: tests reversing a percentage rather than applying one

items.q: If today is Wednesday, what day of the week will it be in 100 days?
What is the output of this Python: print(len([x for x in range(20) if x % 3 == 0]))
Solve for x: 3x + 7 = 2x + 15. Give only the value of x.
A bag has 3 red and 5 blue marbles. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability both are red? Give the answer as a fraction in lowest terms.
How many bytes are in 2.5 kibibytes?
items.why: KiB vs KB — the units trap that motivated this whole protocol

items.q: Put these in ascending order and give only the second smallest: 0.5, 1/3, 0.45, 2/5
items.why: 1/3=0.333 < 2/5=0.4 < 0.45 < 0.5. 'Second smallest' is unambiguous where 'middle value' of an even-length list is not. Accepts 0.4 via judge.

items.q: A train travels 240 km in 3 hours. At the same speed, how many kilometres does it travel in 50 minutes?
items.why: 80 km/h * 5/6 h; accepts 66.7 or 200/3 via judge

items.q: What is the smallest prime number greater than 90?

known_weaknesses: T2-08 originally asked for the 'middle value' of a four-item list, which is ambiguous. Rewritten to 'second smallest' before first use. Recorded because the original would have produced a known-bad score and blamed the model for it.
T2-09 has multiple valid renderings (66.67, 66.7, 200/3). It leans on the judge rather than exact match, which makes it a live test of the judge as well as the model.
Difficulty is asserted, not measured. If a healthy stack scores far from 80-90% on tier 2, the ITEMS are wrong, not necessarily the model.
revision_triggers: A known-good stack fails tier 1 -> the item is broken, not the stack.
Tier 2 lands outside roughly 60-95% on a known-good stack -> recalibrate difficulty.
Any item where the judge and exact match disagree repeatedly -> the gold answer is underspecified.
Any item passed by a stack we KNOW is broken -> it is not discriminative, replace it.
tier_struct failing while tiers 1-2 pass is NOT a fixture bug — it is the expected signature of a quant that is fine for chat and unusable for agentic work. Report it, do not 'fix' it.
notes.negative_control_rationale: T1-05 exists because rejudge.py's docstring records a measured failure: a one-token YES/NO verdict turned a reasoning model into a yes-machine that scored 'Paris' equivalent to 'Berlin'. A fixture with no item whose correct answer is a refusal cannot detect that class of failure at all.

tier_struct.purpose: STRUCTURED OUTPUT / TOOL CALLING. Quantisation damages syntax-exact output before it damages prose, because code and JSON have zero margin for error — one missing brace or a hallucinated key name is a total failure where a slightly-worse sentence is not. CLAUDE.md already records this as the '2-Bit Drunk' failure mode. This tier is graded STRUCTURALLY (parse + schema check), never by string match.
tier_struct.why_early: A model can pass tiers 1-2 on arithmetic and prose while being unusable for agentic work. Anyone deploying a quant for tool use needs this signal before they build on it, not after.

items.q: Reply with ONLY a JSON object, no prose, with exactly these keys: name (string), count (integer), active (boolean). Use name="widget", count=7, active=true.
Reply with ONLY a JSON array containing exactly three objects. Each object must have keys id (integer) and label (string). Use ids 1,2,3 and labels "a","b","c".
Reply with ONLY a JSON object with a nested object under the key config, where config has keys retries (integer, value 3) and timeout_s (number, value 1.5).
Reply with ONLY a JSON object with one key message whose string value is exactly: He said "hello" and left.
items.why: escaping — a quant that mangles quote escaping produces unparseable JSON

items.q: You have a tool: get_weather(city: string, units: string). Call it for Paris in celsius. Reply with ONLY a JSON object of the form {"tool": "...", "arguments": {...}}.
items.why: exact key and function names — hallucinating 'location' for 'city' is the classic quantised tool-call failure

items.q: Reply with ONLY a JSON object with key items whose value is an empty array, and key total whose value is the integer 0.
items.why: empty-collection edge case; models often emit null or omit the key
